scope: Taxation-relevant engineering controls demonstrated by the original generic account-management COBOL. This is not a tax-law implementation or evidence of an ATO system.

groups.title: Balance-enquiry mechanics
groups.taxRelevance: Starting point for an enquiry migration after an approved tax-account field mapping.
groups.limit: The original has one generic balance, no taxpayer, tax type, account identifier, period, or authorization.

groups.title: Credit/debit movement mechanics
groups.taxRelevance: Demonstrates why posting arithmetic, rejection, and state changes need replay evidence.
groups.limit: A legacy CREDIT increases this balance. Do not reinterpret it as a tax payment reducing debt without an authorized domain mapping.

groups.title: Amount representation, validation, and capacity
groups.taxRelevance: Protects amount meaning during modernization; the original recorded quirks make sign, precision, and width risks visible.
groups.limit: The capacity is the original sample's field width, not a statutory or real taxation-office limit.

groups.title: Input and process-lifecycle controls
groups.taxRelevance: Shows how EOF, malformed selections, and unattended execution can break a batch or operator workflow.
groups.limit: There is no real tax batch-file format, scheduler, restart checkpoint, or payment receipt protocol.

groups.title: State lifetime and storage seam
groups.taxRelevance: Separates state preserved within one process from the declared modernized restart/persistence behavior.
groups.limit: Neither the original RAM balance nor the modern single-writer file is a transactional taxation ledger.

unprovenTaxCapabilities: Taxpayer, branch, tax type, period, and PRN/account mapping
Receipt deduplication, idempotent posting, payment reversal, and bank reconciliation
Refund eligibility, cross-account offsetting, assessment, interest, and debt-collection rules
Effective-date/cutoff policy, authorization, audit, and production transaction/recovery semantics
